target_customer: Readers who pay subscriptions or tips, and professional short fiction authors who earn from them
problem: Professional short fiction authors had few ways to earn directly from readers, and general tools like Patreon did not fit short stories.
business_model: Subscription and tipping platform with a 25 percent platform cut and no extra payment processing fees for creators

founders.name: Tanya Breshears
founders.background_notes: YC founder profile describes her as an early Airbnb designer/engineer. No education found.

exit.reason: Founder announced an indefinite hiatus from 2021-08-27, saying subscriptions and payments never let the site pay for itself and that it was probably never sustainable, and that a baby during the pandemic made it untenable.

technical_complexity.rationale: A reading and payments site with author dashboards is standard web and mobile engineering for a solo technical founder.

defensibility.rationale: Value depends on authors and readers gathering in one place, but Patreon and later Substack offered similar tools with larger audiences.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Patreon continued to be where many authors moved serials and fiction, per later author posts. No acquisition of Curious Fictions.

market_need_then: Authors wanted direct reader revenue, and creator subscription platforms were growing in 2017 and 2018, but the paying reader base for short stories proved small.

identity.voice_and_tone: Author friendly, described in press as Patreon for professional authors

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Jane Friedman and Locus Magazine on launch coverage and on closing; authors discussed moving to Patreon.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the genre fiction community and covered by trade press, but never grew a large audience.

outcome_analysis: Curious Fictions launched in 2017 as a Patreon for professional short fiction authors and joined YC in Winter 2018. By August 2021 the founder paused it indefinitely, saying subscriptions and payments never made the site self sustaining. The company had only a little outside funding, so a small paying audience for short stories meant revenue never covered costs, and the founder was a solo operator whose capacity dropped during the pandemic.
notes: curiousfictions.com did not resolve in this environment. Funding: the founder said there was a little outside funding at first, with no amount or investor found. Competitor list left empty: the only named rival is Patreon in the YC tagline, and the dated coverage found was from 2021, after the batch. The Jane Friedman pages show two dates and the full text was paywalled, so the closing reason comes from search snippets of the article and Liptak coverage.
